title: Completed direct sum embeds universally injectively into the product
statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $I\subseteq R$ be an ideal, and assume $R$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. For a set $A$, let $F=\bigoplus_{a\in A}R$ be the module of finitely supported families and let $\widehat F=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}F/I^nF$ be its $I$-adic completion, with componentwise operations. The canonical $R$-linear coordinate map $\iota:\widehat F\to\prod_{a\in A}R$ sends a compatible family of residue classes to its coordinatewise $I$-adic limits. For every $R$-module $Q$, the map $Q\otimes_R\iota:Q\otimes_R\widehat F\to Q\otimes_R\prod_{a\in A}R$ is injective.

proof.text: An element of the inverse limit is a compatible sequence $x_n=(x_{n,\alpha})$ with $x_n$ finitely supported in $\bigoplus_\alpha R/I^n$. Completeness of $R$ gives, for each $\alpha$, a unique $y_\alpha\in R$ reducing to $x_{n,\alpha}$ for every $n$. The finite support of each $x_n$ says that only finitely many $y_\alpha$ are nonzero modulo $I^n$. Conversely, such a family gives a compatible inverse-limit element. Equality is coordinatewise, so the canonical coordinate map $\iota$ is injective.

Fix a finite $R$-module $Q$. Choose a finite presentation $R^{\oplus k}\to R^{\oplus m}\to Q\to0$, and write $q_1,\ldots,q_m$ for the images of the standard generators. Let $\varphi:R^{\oplus k}\to R^{\oplus m}$ be the relation map. If an element represented by finitely many convergent coordinate families $(y_{j,\alpha})_\alpha$ maps to zero in $Q\otimes_R\prod_\alpha R$, then for each $\alpha$ the vector $(y_{1,\alpha},\ldots,y_{m,\alpha})$ lies in $\operatorname{im}(\varphi)$.

Apply the existing Artin--Rees node [lem-weil-pbc-artin-rees] to $N=\operatorname{im}(\varphi)\subseteq R^{\oplus m}$. It gives a constant $c$ such that every relation vector in $(I^rR)^{\oplus m}$ has a preimage in $(I^{r-c}R)^{\oplus k}$ for $r\ge c$. Since the coordinate families are convergent, for each fixed $n$ all but finitely many relation vectors lie in $(I^{n+c}R)^{\oplus m}$; choose their preimages in $(I^nR)^{\oplus k}$, and choose arbitrary preimages for the remaining finitely many coordinates. The resulting preimage families are convergent, so they define an element of $\bigoplus_{l=1}^k\widehat F$ mapping to the original tensor element. Thus $Q\otimes_R\iota$ is injective.

proof.text: The sequence $0\to\widehat F\xrightarrow{\iota}\prod_\alpha R\to\operatorname{Coker}(\iota)\to0$ is exact by Step 1. The existing criterion [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test] says that, over a Noetherian ring, injectivity after tensoring with every finite module is equivalent to universal injectivity. Therefore $\iota$ is universally injective.
